subject: dsa
title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
summary: Grow a window while it stays fixable: window length minus the count of its most common letter must be at most k, so the rest can be replaced. Shrink when it isn't.
problem: Return the length of the longest substring you can make all-identical by replacing at most k characters.

steps.caption: Find the longest substring you can make all-identical by replacing at most k = 1 characters. s = AABABBA.
Slide a window [L, R]. It's valid when (window length minus the count of its most common letter) <= k: the rest can be replaced.
[0..1] = AA: already uniform, 0 replacements needed. Valid. Best length so far: 2.
[0..2] = AAB: most common is A (x2); replace the 1 B. 3 - 2 = 1 <= 1. Valid. Best: 3.
[0..3] = AABA: A appears 3 times; replace the 1 B. 4 - 3 = 1 <= 1. Valid. Best: 4.
[0..4] = AABAB: A appears 3 times, length 5, needing 5 - 3 = 2 replacements > 1. Invalid — shrink L.
No valid window beats length 4 (e.g. AABA -> AAAA with one change). Answer: 4.
